input.quote: 19.2 For fifteen days after delivery, each Deliverable will materially conform to its documentation; after that date Vendor has no correction or refund obligation.
input.rationale: The warranty package is otherwise strong: § 19.1 gives a professional-and-workmanlike services warranty plus a conformance warranty, § 19.3 covers Applicable Law compliance and malicious code, § 19.4 provides repair/re-perform/replace with a refund fallback, and § 19.5 expressly preserves the express warranties from the disclaimer. The failure is duration: § 19.2 caps the Deliverable conformance warranty at fifteen days after delivery and then states Vendor has "no correction or refund obligation," which overrides the unqualified § 19.1 conformance warranty and guts the § 19.4 remedy. Fifteen days is below the fallback floor (90 days software / 30 days services) and, given the fifteen business day acceptance window in § 6.1, the warranty would expire at or before acceptance testing concludes. Minimal edit extends the period to ninety (90) days and deletes the cut-off sentence, pointing to the existing § 19.4 remedy.

proposal.summary: Extend Deliverable conformance warranty from 15 to 90 days and remove the cut-off of correction/refund obligations
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have extended the Deliverable conformance warranty from fifteen days to ninety (90) days and removed the sentence cutting off Vendor's correction and refund obligations, since a 15-day period falls below our minimum warranty duration and effectively expires with the acceptance testing window in Section 6.1. The Section 19.4 repair/replace/refund remedy continues to apply.

ops.newText: For ninety (90) days after delivery, each Deliverable will materially conform to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is set out in Section 19.4.
